qe: A condition where 'Glucose' is found in the urine is called:
e: Glycosuria is a classic sign of Diabetes Mellitus, occurring when blood sugar exceeds the kidney's reabsorption limit.

qe: Which bacterium is responsible for 'Tuberculosis' (TB), a major respiratory disease in India?
e: TB is a bacterial infection that primarily affects the lungs but can spread to other parts of the body.

qe: What is 'BCG' vaccine used for?
e: Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) is the vaccine primarily used against tuberculosis.

qe: The 'DOTS' strategy is associated with the treatment of which disease?
e: Directly Observed Treatment, Short-course (DOTS) is the internationally recommended strategy for TB control.

qe: In 'Infant Respiratory Distress Syndrome' (IRDS), the primary deficiency is of:
e: Premature babies often lack enough surfactant, causing their alveoli to collapse with every breath.

qe: What is 'Cyanosis'?
o: Bluish discoloration of skin due to low oxygen
e: It occurs when deoxygenated hemoglobin levels in the blood rise above 5g//dL.

qe: Which of the following describes 'Oxygen Toxicity'?
o: Damage caused by breathing high partial pressures of oxygen for long periods
e: Too much oxygen can create free radicals that damage the central nervous system and lungs.

qe: The 'Mantoux Test' (Skin test) is used to screen for:
e: It checks for an immune response to Tuberculin protein to see if a person has been exposed to TB.

qe: What is the function of the 'Cilia' in the trachea?
o: Moving mucus and trapped particles upward away from the lungs
e: This is part of the 'Mucociliary Escalator' that keeps the lungs clean.

qe: Which type of 'Lung Cancer' is most strongly linked to tobacco smoking?
e: Small cell lung cancer is almost exclusively found in smokers and is highly aggressive.

qe: What is 'Hypercapnia'?
o: Abnormally high levels of CO2 in the blood
e: Hypercapnia leads to respiratory acidosis and is a major trigger for increased breathing.

qe: The 'Lecithin
e: A ratio of 2:1 or higher indicates that the fetal lungs are mature enough for birth.

qe: Which of the following is the 'Universal form' of energy for cell respiration?
e: Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP) is the molecule that stores and transfers energy in all living cells.

qe: What is 'Hemoptysis'?
o: Coughing up blood from the respiratory tract
e: It is a classic symptom of serious conditions like Tuberculosis or Lung Cancer.

qe: The 'Trachea' divides into right and left primary bronchi at the level of which vertebrae?
e: The point of bifurcation is called the 'Carina', located roughly at the level of the 5th thoracic vertebra.

qe: Which of the following describes 'Cheyne-Stokes' breathing?
o: Cycles of increasing and decreasing breathing followed by apnea
e: Often seen in end-of-life care or severe heart failure.

qe: What is the 'Respiratory Quotient' (RQ) of Protein?
e: Proteins have an intermediate RQ value, lower than carbohydrates but higher than fats.

qe: Which gas is used to dilute Oxygen in the tanks of deep-sea divers to avoid toxicity?
e: Heliox (Helium + Oxygen) is used because helium is less soluble in blood than nitrogen.

qe: The 'Pleural Cavity' normally contains:
o: A thin layer of serous fluid
e: Under normal conditions, there is only enough fluid to act as a lubricant; air in this space is a medical emergency.

qe: What is 'Anaerobic Threshold'?
o: Point during exercise where lactic acid starts to accumulate
e: It marks the intensity of exercise where the body can no longer meet energy demands through aerobic means alone.

qe: Which part of the 'Pharynx' is only respiratory in function (no food passes here)?
e: The nasopharynx is located above the soft palate and serves only as an air passage.

qe: Where does the exchange of gases take place in the lungs?
qh: फेफड़ों में गैसों का आदान-प्रदान कहाँ होता है?
e: Exchange of O2 and CO2 happens in the tiny air sacs called Alveoli. / O2 और CO2 का आदान-प्रदान एल्वियोली नामक छोटी वायु थैलियों में होता है।

qe: तपेदिक (टीबी) और निमोनिया से मुख्य रूप से कौन सा अंग प्रभावित होता है?
qh: Which organ is primarily affected by Tuberculosis (TB) and Pneumonia?
e: Both TB and Pneumonia are bacterial infections that target the respiratory system and lungs. / टीबी और निमोनिया दोनों फेफड़ों के संक्रमण से संबंधित हैं।

qe: 'निमोनिया' और 'टीबी' (Tuberculosis) से मुख्य रूप से कौन सा अंग प्रभावित होता है?
qh: Which organ is primarily affected by 'Pneumonia' and 'Tuberculosis' (TB)?
e: Both Pneumonia and TB cause infections in the Alveoli and tissues of the lungs. / निमोनिया और टीबी दोनों फेफड़ों के संक्रमण से संबंधित हैं।

qe: फेफड़ों में संक्रमण वाली कौन सी बीमारी है जिसमें कवक के कारण भारी खांसी होती है?
qh: Which disease involves an infection in the lungs where fungus causes severe coughing?
e: Asthma (Dama) can be triggered or caused by fungal spores irritating the lungs. / दमा फेफड़ों में कवक के कारण हो सकता है।

qe: 'हाइपोक्सिया' (Hypoxia) क्या है?
qh: What is 'Hypoxia'?
o: Oxygen deficiency in tissues | ऊतकों में ऑक्सीजन की कमी
e: Hypoxia is a condition in which the body or a region of it is deprived of adequate oxygen. / हाइपोक्सिया वह स्थिति है जिसमें शरीर को पर्याप्त ऑक्सीजन नहीं मिल पाती।

qe: 'हाइपोक्सिया' (Hypoxia) का सामान्य अर्थ क्या है?
qh: What is the common term for the medical condition 'Hypoxia'?
o: Oxygen deficiency in tissues | ऊतकों में ऑक्सीजन की कमी
e: Hypoxia is a state where oxygen supply is inadequate at the tissue level. / हाइपोक्सिया वह स्थिति है जहाँ ऊतक स्तर पर ऑक्सीजन की आपूर्ति अपर्याप्त होती है।

qe: कीड़े मुख्य रूप से अपने शरीर के किस भाग से सांस लेते हैं?
qh: Insects primarily breathe through which part of their body?
e: Insects use a tracheal system of tubes to transport oxygen directly to tissues. / कीड़े ऊतकों तक सीधे ऑक्सीजन पहुँचाने के लिए ट्रेकिया नलियों का उपयोग करते हैं।

qe: अधिक ऊंचाई पर, रक्त में ऑक्सीजन के कम स्तर के कारण कौन सी स्थिति उत्पन्न होती है?
qh: At high altitudes, what condition occurs due to low oxygen levels in the blood?
e: Hypoxia is the deficiency of oxygen reaching the tissues. / हाइपोक्सिया ऊतकों तक पहुँचने वाली ऑक्सीजन की कमी है।

qe: कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड (CO2) और जलवाष्प के उत्सर्जन के लिए कौन सा अंग जिम्मेदार है?
qh: Which organ is responsible for the excretion of Carbon Dioxide (CO2) and water vapor?
e: Lungs excrete gaseous waste like CO2 and moisture. / फेफड़े CO2 और नमी जैसे गैसीय कचरे का उत्सर्जन करते हैं।

qe: 'हाइपोक्सिया' (Hypoxia) के दौरान क्या होता है?
qh: What happens during 'Hypoxia'?
o: Oxygen deficiency in tissues | ऊतकों में ऑक्सीजन की कमी
e: Hypoxia is a condition where body tissues do not receive enough oxygen. / हाइपोक्सिया वह स्थिति है जहाँ शरीर के ऊतकों को पर्याप्त ऑक्सीजन नहीं मिलती है।

qe: कौन सी गैस ली गई हवा में 21% होती है लेकिन छोड़ी गई हवा में 17% होती है?
qh: Which gas is found in inhaled air at 21% but exhaled at 17%?
e: Cells use about 4% of the inhaled oxygen during respiration. / कोशिकाएं श्वसन के दौरान ली गई लगभग 4% ऑक्सीजन का उपयोग करती हैं।

qe: किस गैस का हीमोग्लोबिन के प्रति आकर्षण ऑक्सीजन से 200 गुना अधिक होता है?
qh: Which gas has 200 times more affinity for hemoglobin than oxygen?
e: Carbon Monoxide binds to hemoglobin very strongly, preventing oxygen transport. / कार्बन मोनोऑक्साइड हीमोग्लोबिन से बहुत मजबूती से जुड़ती है, जिससे ऑक्सीजन परिवहन रुक जाता है।

qe: ट्रेकिया में 'C-आकार' के हलीन कार्टिलेज का क्या कार्य है?
qh: What is the function of the 'C-shaped' hyaline cartilage in the Trachea?
e: Hyaline cartilage provides structural support to keep the windpipe open. / हलीन कार्टिलेज श्वास नली को खुला रखने के लिए संरचनात्मक सहायता प्रदान करता है।

qe: 'हाइपोक्सिया' (Hypoxia) क्या है?
qh: What is 'Hypoxia'?
o: Low oxygen in tissues | ऊतकों में ऑक्सीजन की कमी
e: Hypoxia occurs when tissues do not receive enough oxygen, common at high altitudes. / हाइपोक्सिया तब होता है जब ऊतकों को पर्याप्त ऑक्सीजन नहीं मिलती, जो ऊंचाई पर आम है।

qe: किस गैस को 'साइलेंट किलर' कहा जाता है क्योंकि यह ऑक्सीजन की तुलना में हीमोग्लोबिन से बहुत तेजी से जुड़ती है?
qh: Which gas is known as the 'silent killer' because it binds to hemoglobin much faster than oxygen?
e: CO binds to hemoglobin 200 times more strongly than oxygen, causing suffocation. / CO ऑक्सीजन की तुलना में हीमोग्लोबिन से 200 गुना अधिक मजबूती से जुड़ती है।

qe: ऊंचाई के कारण ऊतकों में ऑक्सीजन की कमी की स्थिति ____ कहलाती है।
qh: The condition of oxygen deficiency in tissues due to high altitude is called ____.
e: Hypoxia occurs when there is a low supply of oxygen at the tissue level. / हाइपोक्सिया तब होता है जब ऊतक स्तर पर ऑक्सीजन की आपूर्ति कम होती है।

qe: कौन सी गैस हीमोग्लोबिन के प्रति अत्यधिक आकर्षक है और विषाक्तता का कारण बनती है?
qh: Which gas is highly attractive to hemoglobin and causes poisoning?
e: CO binds 200 times faster to hemoglobin than oxygen, causing suffocation. / CO ऑक्सीजन की तुलना में हीमोग्लोबिन से 200 गुना तेजी से जुड़ता है।

qe: कोविड के दौरान फेफड़ों की क्षति की जांच के लिए किस प्रकार के सीटी स्कैन का उपयोग किया गया था?
qh: Which type of CT scan was used to check lung damage during COVID?
e: HRCT (High Resolution Computed Tomography) shows detailed damage in lung lobes. / HRCT फेफड़ों के लोभ में विस्तृत क्षति को दर्शाता है।

qe: मानव के 'बाएं फेफड़े' में कितने लोभ (भाग) होते हैं?
qh: How many 'Lobes' are present in the 'Left Lung' of a human?
e: The left lung has 2 lobes, while the right lung has 3. / बाएं फेफड़े में 2 लोभ होते हैं, जबकि दाएं में 3 होते हैं।

qe: श्वसन के दौरान उपयोग की गई पहली 4% ऑक्सीजन किसमें बदल जाती है?
qh: The first 4% of Oxygen consumed during respiration is converted into ____.
e: Cells use oxygen and release carbon dioxide as a waste product. / कोशिकाएं ऑक्सीजन का उपयोग करती हैं और अपशिष्ट उत्पाद के रूप में CO2 छोड़ती हैं।

qe: 'कार्बन मोनोऑक्साइड' (CO), CO2 से अधिक खतरनाक क्यों है?
qh: Why is 'Carbon Monoxide' (CO) more dangerous than CO2?
o: Hemoglobin loves it more than Oxygen | हीमोग्लोबिन इसे ऑक्सीजन से ज्यादा पसंद करता है
e: Hemoglobin binds to CO 200 times faster than oxygen, causing suffocation. / हीमोग्लोबिन ऑक्सीजन की तुलना में CO से 200 गुना तेजी से जुड़ता है।

qe: मानव फेफड़ों में कुल कितने 'लोभ' (भाग) होते हैं?
qh: How many 'Lobes' are there in total in human Lungs?
e: Right lung has 3 lobes and left lung has 2, totaling 5. / दाएं फेफड़े में 3 और बाएं में 2, कुल 5 लोभ होते हैं।

qe: किस गैस का हीमोग्लोबिन के प्रति आकर्षण ऑक्सीजन से अधिक होता है?
qh: Which gas has a higher affinity for hemoglobin than oxygen?
e: Carbon Monoxide binds to hemoglobin 200 times more strongly than oxygen. / कार्बन मोनोऑक्साइड हीमोग्लोबिन से ऑक्सीजन की तुलना में 200 गुना अधिक मजबूती से जुड़ती है।

qe: निःश्वसन (सांस छोड़ने) के दौरान, छोड़े गए CO2 का अनुमानित प्रतिशत क्या है?
qh: During exhalation (Nih-swasan), what is the approximate percentage of CO2 released?
e: Inhaled air has 0.03% CO2, but exhaled air contains about 4% CO2. / ली गई हवा में 0.03% CO2 होती है, लेकिन छोड़ी गई हवा में लगभग 4% CO2 होती है।

qe: 'आंतरिक श्वसन' या कोशिकीय श्वसन कहाँ होता है?
qh: Where does 'Internal Respiration' or Cellular Respiration take place?
e: Respiration occurring inside the cell to produce energy is called internal or cellular respiration. / ऊर्जा उत्पादन के लिए कोशिका के अंदर होने वाले श्वसन को आंतरिक या कोशिकीय श्वसन कहा जाता है।

qe: कोशिका द्रव में होने वाले ग्लूकोज विखंडन के पहले चरण को क्या कहा जाता है?
qh: The first step of glucose breakdown that occurs in the Cytoplasm is called ____.
e: Glycolysis is the process of breaking down glucose into pyruvic acid in the cytoplasm. / ग्लाइकोलाइसिस कोशिका द्रव में ग्लूकोज को पाइरुविक एसिड में तोड़ने की प्रक्रिया है।

qe: ग्लाइकोलाइसिस प्रक्रिया के दौरान कुल कितने एटीपी (ATP) अणुओं का लाभ होता है?
qh: How many net ATP molecules are gained during the Glycolysis process?
e: Total 4 ATP are produced, but 2 are consumed in the process, leaving a net gain of 2 ATP. / कुल 4 एटीपी बनते हैं, लेकिन 2 खर्च हो जाते हैं, जिससे शुद्ध लाभ 2 एटीपी का होता है।

qe: ग्लूकोज का एक अणु बनाने के लिए कितने एटीपी अणुओं की आवश्यकता होती है?
qh: How many ATP molecules are required to form one molecule of Glucose?
e: 38 ATP molecules combine to provide the energy equivalent of one glucose molecule. / एक ग्लूकोज अणु के बराबर ऊर्जा प्रदान करने के लिए 38 एटीपी अणु मिलते हैं।

qe: ग्लाइकोलाइसिस और क्रैब चक्र के बीच कड़ी के रूप में कौन सा अणु कार्य करता है?
qh: Which molecule acts as a link between Glycolysis and the Krebs Cycle?
e: Acetyl-CoA carries the breakdown product of glucose into the Krebs cycle. / एसिटिल को-एंजाइम ग्लूकोज के विखंडन उत्पाद को क्रैब चक्र में ले जाता है।

qe: ऑक्सीजन की अनुपस्थिति में ग्लूकोज का टूटना ____ कहलाता है।
qh: The breakdown of glucose in the absence of oxygen is called ____.
e: Anaerobic respiration occurs without oxygen, primarily in the cytoplasm. / अनॉक्सी श्वसन ऑक्सीजन के बिना होता है, मुख्य रूप से कोशिका द्रव में।

qe: शरीर के ऊतकों में ऑक्सीजन की कमी को क्या कहा जाता है?
qh: Which condition refers to a deficiency of oxygen in body tissues?
e: Hypoxia is a state where the body or a region of the body is deprived of adequate oxygen supply. / हाइपोक्सिया वह स्थिति है जहाँ शरीर या उसके किसी हिस्से को पर्याप्त ऑक्सीजन नहीं मिल पाती है।

qe: किस गैस का हीमोग्लोबिन के प्रति आकर्षण ऑक्सीजन से बहुत अधिक होता है, जिससे विषाक्तता होती है?
qh: Which gas has a much higher affinity for hemoglobin than oxygen, leading to poisoning?
e: Carbon Monoxide binds to hemoglobin 200 times more strongly than oxygen. / कार्बन मोनोऑक्साइड ऑक्सीजन की तुलना में हीमोग्लोबिन से 200 गुना अधिक मजबूती से जुड़ती है।

qe: श्वसन के दौरान 'डायफ्राम' का मुख्य कार्य क्या है?
qh: What is the primary function of the 'Diaphragm' during respiration?
o: Create pressure to inhale/exhale | सांस लेने/छोड़ने के लिए दबाव बनाना
e: The diaphragm contracts and flattens to expand the chest cavity for inhalation. / डायफ्राम सिकुड़ता है और सांस लेने के लिए छाती की गुहा का विस्तार करने हेतु चपटा हो जाता है।

qe: नाक में छोटे बालों जैसे फिल्टर ____ में स्थित होते हैं।
qh: The small hair-like filters in the nose are located in the ____.
e: Nasal hairs trap large dust particles before air moves deeper. / हवा के गहराई में जाने से पहले नासा रोम बड़े धूल कणों को पकड़ लेते हैं।

qe: कीड़े मुख्य रूप से अपने शरीर के किस भाग से सांस लेते हैं?
qh: Insects primarily breathe through which part of their body?
e: Insects have a network of tracheal tubes for direct gas exchange. / कीड़ों में सीधे गैस विनिमय के लिए ट्रेकिया नलियों का एक जाल होता है।

qe: एक 'टेडपोल' (मेंढक का बच्चा) ____ का उपयोग करके श्वसन करता है।
qh: A 'Tadpole' (baby frog) respires using ____.
e: Tadpoles live in water and have gills, which are replaced by lungs in adults. / टेडपोल पानी में रहते हैं और उनमें गिल्स होते हैं, जो वयस्कों में फेफड़ों द्वारा बदल दिए जाते हैं।

qe: जीवित शरीर निरंतर ऊष्मा क्यों उत्पन्न करता है?
qh: Why does a living body generate heat continuously?
o: Due to cellular respiration | कोशिकीय श्वसन के कारण
e: Cellular respiration in mitochondria releases heat as a byproduct. / माइट्रोकांड्रिया में कोशिकीय श्वसन के दौरान ऊष्मा एक सह-उत्पाद के रूप में निकलती है।

qe: फेफड़ों की वह मुख्य कार्यात्मक इकाई क्या है जहाँ गैसों का आदान-प्रदान होता है?
qh: What is the primary functional unit of the lungs where gas exchange occurs?
e: Alveoli are tiny air sacs where oxygen enters the blood and CO2 leaves it. / एल्वियोली छोटी वायु थैलियां हैं जहां ऑक्सीजन रक्त में प्रवेश करती है और CO2 बाहर निकलती है।

qe: मनुष्यों में 'वॉइस बॉक्स' (स्वर यंत्र) को ____ कहा जाता है।
qh: The 'Voice Box' in humans is known as ____.
e: The larynx is responsible for sound production in humans. / लैरिंग्स मनुष्यों में ध्वनि उत्पादन के लिए जिम्मेदार है।

qe: मानव के 'दाएं फेफड़े' में कितने लोभ (भाग) होते हैं?
qh: How many lobes are present in the 'Right Lung' of a human?
e: The right lung has 3 lobes, while the left lung has 2 to accommodate the heart. / दाएं फेफड़े में 3 लोभ होते हैं, जबकि बाएं फेफड़े में हृदय के लिए जगह बनाने हेतु 2 लोभ होते हैं।

qe: ____ की उपस्थिति के कारण बायां फेफड़ा दाएं फेफड़े से थोड़ा छोटा होता है।
qh: The left lung is slightly smaller than the right lung because of the presence of ____.
e: The heart is tilted towards the left, leaving less space for the left lung. / हृदय बाईं ओर झुका होता है, जिससे बाएं फेफड़े के लिए कम जगह बचती है।

qe: विशेष रूप से फेफड़ों की स्थिति की जांच के लिए किस प्रकार के सीटी स्कैन का उपयोग किया जाता है?
qh: Which type of CT scan is specifically used to check the condition of the lungs (common during COVID)?
e: HRCT (High-Resolution Computed Tomography) provides detailed images of lung lobes. / HRCT फेफड़ों के लोभ की विस्तृत छवियां प्रदान करता है।

qe: 'श्वास नली' का चिकित्सा नाम क्या है?
qh: What is the medical name for the 'Windpipe'?
e: The trachea is the main tube connecting the larynx to the bronchi. / ट्रेकिया मुख्य नली है जो लैरिंग्स को ब्रोंकाई से जोड़ती है।

qe: ट्रेकिया को पचकने से रोकने के लिए C-आकार के छल्ले किसके बने होते हैं?
qh: The trachea is prevented from collapsing by C-shaped rings made of ____.
e: Hyaline cartilage provides structural support to keep the windpipe open. / हलीन कार्टिलेज श्वास नली को खुला रखने के लिए संरचनात्मक सहायता प्रदान करता है।

qe: HRCT फेफड़ों की रिपोर्ट में दी जाने वाली अधिकतम रेटिंग स्कोर क्या है?
qh: What is the maximum rating score given in an HRCT lung report?
e: Each of the 5 lobes is rated out of 5, making a total of 25. / 5 लोभों में से प्रत्येक को 5 में से रेटिंग दी जाती है, जिससे कुल 25 हो जाता है।

qe: एक 'वेंटिलेटर' उस रोगी के लिए कृत्रिम ____ के रूप में कार्य करता है जो सांस नहीं ले सकता।
qh: A 'Ventilator' acts as an artificial ____ for a patient who cannot breathe.
e: Ventilators mechanically pump air into the lungs when the diaphragm or lungs fail. / वेंटिलेटर यांत्रिक रूप से फेफड़ों में हवा पंप करते हैं जब डायफ्राम या फेफड़े काम नहीं करते।

qe: पक्षियों में ध्वनि उत्पन्न करने वाले अंग का नाम क्या है?
qh: What is the name of the sound-producing organ in birds?
e: Birds use the syrinx located at the base of the trachea to produce sound. / पक्षी ध्वनि उत्पन्न करने के लिए ट्रेकिया के आधार पर स्थित सिरिंक्स (शेरिंग्स) का उपयोग करते हैं।

qe: 'एडम्स एप्पल' पुरुषों में किस अंग का उभरा हुआ हिस्सा है?
qh: The 'Adam's Apple' is a prominent part of which organ in males?
e: The Adam's apple is the protrusion of the thyroid cartilage surrounding the larynx. / एडम्स एप्पल लैरिंग्स के चारों ओर थायराइड कार्टिलेज का उभार है।

qe: कीड़े मुख्य रूप से अपनी ____ से सांस लेते हैं।
qh: Insects primarily breathe through their ____.
e: Insects have a tracheal system that delivers oxygen directly to tissues. / कीड़ों में एक ट्रेकिया प्रणाली होती है जो ऑक्सीजन को सीधे ऊतकों तक पहुँचाती है।

qe: फेफड़ों के नीचे की कौन सी मांसपेशियों की चादर सांस लेने और छोड़ने में मदद करती है?
qh: Which muscular sheet below the lungs helps in inhalation and exhalation?
e: The diaphragm is the primary muscle responsible for breathing. / डायफ्राम सांस लेने के लिए जिम्मेदार प्राथमिक मांसपेशी है।

qe: भोजन और वायु दोनों के लिए सामान्य मार्ग कौन सा है?
qh: What is the common passage for both food and air?
e: The pharynx is the common space where both the oral and nasal cavities meet. / ग्रसनी वह सामान्य स्थान है जहाँ मौखिक और नासा गुहा दोनों मिलते हैं।

qe: फेफड़ों में हवा लेने की प्रक्रिया को क्या कहा जाता है?
qh: The process of taking air into the lungs is called ____.
e: Inhalation is the intake of air rich in oxygen into the body. / निश््वसन शरीर में ऑक्सीजन युक्त हवा लेने की क्रिया है।

qe: स्वाच्छोवास (Breathing) निश््वसन और ____ का संयोजन है।
qh: Breathing is a combination of Inhalation and ____.
e: Breathing involves both breathing in (inhalation) and breathing out (exhalation). / स्वाच्छोवास में सांस लेना और छोड़ना दोनों शामिल हैं।

qe: शरीर में ऑक्सीजन लेने का मुख्य उद्देश्य क्या है?
qh: What is the primary purpose of taking Oxygen into the body?
o: To break down Glucose in Mitochondria | माइट्रोकांड्रिया में ग्लूकोज को तोड़ना
e: Oxygen is used in cellular respiration to release energy from glucose. / कोशिकीय श्वसन में ग्लूकोज से ऊर्जा मुक्त करने के लिए ऑक्सीजन का उपयोग किया जाता है।

qe: श्वसन को किस प्रकार की चयापचय प्रक्रिया माना जाता है?
qh: Respiration is considered which type of metabolic process?
e: Respiration is a destructive (breaking down) process, hence it is catabolic. / श्वसन एक विनाशकारी (तोड़ने वाली) प्रक्रिया है, इसलिए यह कैटाबॉलिक है।

qe: मृत शरीर कुछ समय बाद ठंडा क्यों हो जाता है?
qh: Why does a dead body become cold after some time?
o: Stoppage of respiration and heat production | श्वसन और ऊष्मा उत्पादन का रुकना
e: Respiration generates heat; when it stops, the body loses its ability to maintain 37°C. / श्वसन से ऊष्मा उत्पन्न होती है; जब यह रुक जाता है, तो शरीर 37°C बनाए रखने की क्षमता खो देता है।

qe: श्वसन के दौरान कितनी नाइट्रोजन बाहर छोड़ी जाती है?
qh: How much Nitrogen is exhaled during breathing?
e: Nitrogen is not used by the body, so 78% inhaled is 78% exhaled. / नाइट्रोजन का शरीर द्वारा उपयोग नहीं किया जाता है, इसलिए 78% ली गई हवा 78% ही बाहर निकलती है।

qe: छोड़ी गई हवा में ऑक्सीजन का प्रतिशत कितना होता है?
qh: What is the percentage of Oxygen in exhaled air?
e: We inhale 21% oxygen but exhale about 17% after some is used by cells. / हम 21% ऑक्सीजन लेते हैं लेकिन कोशिकाओं द्वारा कुछ उपयोग किए जाने के बाद लगभग 17% छोड़ते हैं।

qe: छोड़ी गई हवा में लगभग कितना कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड (CO2) मौजूद होता है?
qh: Approximately how much Carbon Dioxide (CO2) is present in exhaled air?
e: The used 4% oxygen is converted and exhaled as CO2. / उपयोग की गई 4% ऑक्सीजन को CO2 के रूप में परिवर्तित और बाहर निकाला जाता है।

qe: मछली जैसे जलीय जंतुओं के लिए श्वसन अंग क्या है?
qh: What is the respiratory organ for aquatic animals like Fish?
e: Fish use gills to extract dissolved oxygen from water. / मछली पानी से घुली हुई ऑक्सीजन निकालने के लिए गिल्स का उपयोग करती है।

qe: कीड़े नलियों के एक जाल के माध्यम से श्वसन करते हैं जिन्हें ____ कहा जाता है।
qh: Insects respire through a network of tubes called ____.
e: Insects have a tracheal system that carries oxygen directly to their tissues. / कीड़ों में एक ट्रेकिया प्रणाली होती है जो ऑक्सीजन को सीधे उनके ऊतकों तक ले जाती है।

qe: एक 'टेडपोल' (मेंढक का बच्चा) श्वसन के लिए किसका उपयोग करता है?
qh: What does a 'Tadpole' (baby frog) use for respiration?
e: Tadpoles live in water and use gills, which disappear as they become adult frogs. / टेडपोल पानी में रहते हैं और गिल्स का उपयोग करते हैं, जो वयस्क मेंढक बनने पर गायब हो जाते हैं।

qe: जमीन पर रहने के दौरान एक वयस्क मेंढक श्वसन के लिए किस अंग का उपयोग करता है?
qh: Which organ does an adult frog use for respiration while on land?
e: On land, adult frogs primarily use their lungs for breathing. / जमीन पर, वयस्क मेंढक मुख्य रूप से सांस लेने के लिए अपने फेफड़ों का उपयोग करते हैं।

qe: जब मेंढक मिट्टी के नीचे गहरा दबा होता है (निष्क्रियता), तो वह कैसे सांस लेता है?
qh: How does a frog breathe when it is buried deep under the soil (Hibernation)?
e: Frogs can absorb oxygen through their moist skin during hibernation. / मेंढक सुप्तावस्था के दौरान अपनी नम त्वचा के माध्यम से ऑक्सीजन सोख सकते हैं।

qe: 'हिचकी' का सामान्य कारण क्या है?
qh: What is the common cause of 'Hiccups' (Hichki) ?
o: Diaphragm irritation or food blockage | डायफ्राम में हलचल या भोजन का अटकना
e: Hiccups often occur when the diaphragm is forced to push air/food, or due to a mismatch in signals. / हिचकी अक्सर तब आती है जब डायफ्राम को हवा/भोजन धकेलने के लिए मजबूर किया जाता है।

qe: श्वसन की दर को मापने के लिए किस उपकरण का उपयोग किया जाता है?
qh: Which instrument is used to measure the rate of respiration?
e: A respirometer measures the rate of exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide. / रेस्पिरोमीटर ऑक्सीजन और कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड के विनिमय की दर को मापता है।

qe: किस गैस का प्रतिशत लेने और छोड़ने वाली हवा में समान होता है?
qh: Which gas has the same percentage in both inhaled and exhaled air?
e: Since Nitrogen is not consumed, 78% is taken in and 78% is breathed out. / चूंकि नाइट्रोजन की खपत नहीं होती है, इसलिए 78% अंदर ली जाती है और 78% बाहर छोड़ी जाती है।

qe: यदि भोजन गलती से 'श्वास नली' (ट्रेकिया) में चला जाए तो क्या होता है?
qh: What happens if food accidentally enters the 'Windpipe' (Trachea)?
o: Coughing or Choking (Surakana) | सरकना या खांसी आना
e: The body reflexively forces air out (hiccup or cough) to remove the foreign object from the windpipe. / श्वास नली से बाहरी वस्तु को निकालने के लिए शरीर अनैच्छिक रूप से हवा बाहर निकालता है।

qe: What is the main waste product of human respiration? / मानव श्वसन का मुख्य अपशिष्ट उत्पाद क्या है?
e: Humans inhale Oxygen and exhale Carbon Dioxide. / मनुष्य ऑक्सीजन लेते हैं और कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड छोड़ते हैं।

qe: During exhalation, the diaphragm moves: / उच्छ्वास (साँस छोड़ने) के दौरान, डायाफ्राम:
e: During exhalation, the diaphragm relaxes and moves up. / साँस छोड़ने के दौरान, डायाफ्राम शिथिल होकर ऊपर की ओर बढ़ता है।

qe: Which of the following is the 'Primary Site' of gas exchange in the human lungs?
e: Alveoli are tiny air sacs with thin walls and a large surface area, allowing oxygen to enter the blood and CO2 to leave.

qe: The 'Voice Box' in the human respiratory system is scientifically known as the:
e: The larynx contains vocal cords that vibrate to produce sound when air passes through.

qe: Which structure prevents food from entering the trachea (windpipe) during swallowing?
e: The epiglottis is a flap of elastic cartilage that covers the larynx when you swallow.

qe: What is the normal breathing rate of a healthy adult at rest?
e: Adults typically breathe about 12 to 16 times per minute under normal conditions.

qe: Which muscle is the most important for the process of 'Inspiration' (Inhaling)?
e: When the diaphragm contracts and flattens, it increases the volume of the chest cavity, pulling air into the lungs.

qe: What is 'Tidal Volume' (TV)?
o: Volume of air inspired or expired during a normal breath
Maximum air one can breathe out
Air left in lungs after a forceful breath
e: In a healthy adult, the Tidal Volume is approximately 500 ml per breath.

qe: The majority of 'Carbon Dioxide' (CO2) is transported in the blood as:
e: About 70% of CO2 is carried in the form of bicarbonate ions in the plasma.

qe: Which pigment in humans has a higher affinity for oxygen than adult hemoglobin?
e: Fetal hemoglobin must pull oxygen from the mother's blood, and myoglobin stores oxygen in muscles; both bind O2 more tightly.

qe: What is 'Residual Volume' (RV)?
o: Volume of air remaining in lungs even after a forceful expiration
Volume of air in the trachea
e: Residual volume ensures that the lungs do not collapse and allows for continuous gas exchange.

qe: Which instrument is used to measure 'Lung Volumes' and pulmonary function?
e: Spirometry is the standard test used to diagnose conditions like Asthma and COPD.

qe: A condition where the alveolar walls are damaged, reducing the surface area for gas exchange, is called:
e: Emphysema is commonly caused by long-term smoking and makes it very difficult to breathe.

qe: Which part of the brain contains the 'Respiratory Rhythm Center'?
e: The medulla oblongata regulates the automatic rhythm of breathing.

qe: What is the 'Chloride Shift' (Hamburger's phenomenon) related to?
o: CO2 transport and ionic balance in RBCs
e: It is the movement of chloride ions into RBCs to maintain electrical neutrality when bicarbonate leaves.

qe: The 'Vital Capacity' (VC) of the lungs is the sum of:
e: VC represents the maximum amount of air a person can expel from the lungs after a maximum inhalation.

qe: Which gas has an affinity for hemoglobin that is 200-250 times higher than oxygen?
e: CO binds so tightly to hemoglobin that it prevents oxygen transport, leading to carbon monoxide poisoning.

qe: What is 'Pneumonia'?
o: Infection causing fluid accumulation in alveoli
e: Pneumonia is an inflammatory condition of the lung affecting primarily the microscopic air sacs.

qe: Which layer of the 'Pleura' is in direct contact with the lung surface?
e: The visceral pleura covers the lungs, while the parietal pleura lines the chest wall.

qe: The exchange of gases between the blood and the body tissues is called:
e: Internal respiration is the unloading of O2 and loading of CO2 at the tissue level.

qe: What is the function of 'Surfactant' in the alveoli?
o: Prevent alveoli from collapsing during expiration
e: Surfactant reduces surface tension, making it easier for the lungs to expand.

qe: Which chemical factor is the most powerful stimulant for breathing in a healthy person?
o: High Carbon Dioxide levels (and low pH)
e: The brain is much more sensitive to CO2 buildup than to O2 lack when regulating normal breathing.

qe: Which of the following describes the 'Bohr Effect'?
o: Low pH and high CO2 decrease Hemoglobin's affinity for O2
High O2 displaces CO2 from blood
e: The Bohr effect ensures that active tissues (which produce CO2 and acid) get more oxygen released from hemoglobin.

qe: The 'Haldane Effect' is primarily concerned with the transport of:
e: It states that deoxygenated hemoglobin has a higher affinity for CO2, helping the blood pick up waste from tissues.

qe: What is the 'Vital Capacity' (VC) of a healthy adult male?
e: Vital Capacity is the maximum amount of air one can exhale after a maximum inhalation.

qe: Which enzyme in RBCs is responsible for the rapid conversion of CO2 and water into Carbonic Acid?
e: Carbonic anhydrase is one of the fastest enzymes in the body, essential for CO2 transport as bicarbonate.

qe: The 'Pneumotaxic Center' which limits the duration of inspiration is located in:
e: While the rhythm center is in the medulla, the 'switch-off' point for breathing is in the pons.

qe: What is the 'Dead Space' volume in the human respiratory tract?
e: Anatomic dead space is the volume of air in the conducting zone (trachea, bronchi) that does not participate in gas exchange.

qe: Which shape does the 'Oxygen-Hemoglobin Dissociation Curve' typically take?
e: The sigmoid shape is due to 'cooperative binding,' where the binding of one O2 molecule makes it easier for others to bind.

qe: A 'Right Shift' in the Oxygen-Dissociation curve is caused by:
e: Factors like high temperature, high CO2, and high 2,3-DPG shift the curve to the right, meaning O2 is released more easily.

qe: The condition 'Mountain Sickness' (Altitude Sickness) is primarily caused by:
o: Low percentage of Oxygen in air
e: At high altitudes, the total air pressure is low, which reduces the driving force (pO2) for oxygen to enter the blood.

qe: What is 'Hyperpnea'?
o: Increased depth and rate of breathing during exercise
e: Hyperpnea is a normal physiological response to meet the increased oxygen demand of the body.

qe: Which cell in the Alveoli secretes 'Surfactant'?
e: Type II cells produce surfactant (lecithin) to prevent the lungs from collapsing.

qe: The 'Hering-Breuer Reflex' prevents:
e: Stretch receptors in the lungs signal the brain to stop inspiration if the lungs are stretched too much.

qe: Which of the following is an 'Occupational Respiratory Disorder'?
e: Silicosis and Asbestosis occur in workers exposed to dust in stone-breaking or construction industries.

qe: What is 'Functional Residual Capacity' (FRC)?
e: FRC is the volume of air remaining in the lungs after a normal (tidal) expiration.

qe: In which form is 20-25% of Carbon Dioxide transported in the blood?
e: CO2 binds directly to the globin part of the hemoglobin molecule, not the iron center.

qe: Which part of the respiratory system is known as the 'Conducting Zone'?
e: The conducting zone filters, warms, and humidifies air but does not participate in gas exchange.

qe: What is the partial pressure of Oxygen ($pO_{2}$) in the deoxygenated blood?
e: Deoxygenated blood has a $pO_{2}$ of 40 mmHg and a $pCO_{2}$ of 45 mmHg.

qe: Which structure 'zips' the trachea open with C-shaped rings of cartilage?
e: Hyaline cartilage rings prevent the trachea from collapsing under the negative pressure of breathing.

qe: What is 'Dyspnea'?
e: Dyspnea is often described as 'shortness of breath' and is a common symptom of heart and lung disease.

qe: The 'Respiratory Membrane' (Diffusion membrane) consists of how many main layers?
e: It consists of the alveolar epithelium, the capillary endothelium, and the fused basement membrane in between.

qe: Which of the following animals performs 'Cutaneous Respiration' (breathing through the skin)?
e: Earthworms use their moist skin for gas exchange, which is why they die if their skin dries out.

qe: The respiratory organs in insects like 'Cockroaches' are called:
e: Insects have a network of tubes that deliver oxygen directly to the tissues, bypassing the blood.

qe: Which structure in 'Birds' makes their respiratory system the most efficient among vertebrates?
e: Air sacs allow for a continuous, one-way flow of fresh air through the lungs during both inhalation and exhalation.

qe: The 'Pneumatic Center' of the brain that controls the switch from inspiration to expiration is the:
e: Specifically, the pneumotaxic center in the pons limits the duration of inspiration to regulate the rate of breathing.

qe: What is 'Hypoxia'?
o: Lack of adequate oxygen supply at the tissue level
e: Hypoxia can result from low atmospheric oxygen, anemia, or poor circulation.

qe: Which of the following is a symptom of 'Carbon Monoxide' poisoning?
e: CO-hemoglobin (Carboxyhemoglobin) is bright red, giving the skin a characteristic flush even as the person suffocates.

qe: The 'Pleural Fluid' found between the lung membranes serves what purpose?
e: The fluid acts as a lubricant, allowing the lungs to slide smoothly against the chest wall.

qe: What is 'Inspiratory Capacity' (IC)?
e: IC is the total volume of air a person can breathe in starting from a normal expiration level.

qe: Which part of the 'Hemoglobin' molecule does $CO_{2}$ bind to?
e: Unlike oxygen, which binds to iron, CO2 binds to the protein part, forming carbamino-hemoglobin.

qe: What is 'Apnea'?
e: Sleep apnea is a common disorder where breathing repeatedly stops and starts during sleep.

qe: The 'Dust Cells' found in the alveoli are actually:
e: Alveolar macrophages (dust cells) clean the lungs by engulfing dust particles and bacteria.

qe: Which condition is characterized by a 'Wheezing' sound during expiration due to inflammation of bronchi?
e: Asthma is an allergic reaction that causes spasms in the smooth muscles of the bronchioles.

qe: The 'Total Lung Capacity' (TLC) is roughly ________ in an average adult male.
e: TLC includes the Vital Capacity plus the Residual Volume (the air you can never breathe out).

qe: Which nerve carries the signal from the brain to the 'Diaphragm' to initiate breathing?
e: Irritation of the phrenic nerve is often the cause of hiccups.

qe: What happens to the 'Diaphragm' during Exhalation (breathing out)?
e: Relaxation of the diaphragm decreases the chest volume, forcing air out of the lungs.

qe: Which of the following describes 'Asphyxia'?
o: Extreme decrease in oxygen and increase in CO2 in the body
e: Asphyxia leads to unconsciousness and death if not treated immediately.

qe: The 'Adam's Apple' is formed by which cartilage of the larynx?
e: The thyroid cartilage is larger in males due to testosterone, creating the visible Adam's apple.

qe: What is 'Partial Pressure' of a gas?
o: Pressure contributed by an individual gas in a mixture
e: Gases always diffuse from an area of high partial pressure to low partial pressure.

qe: Which type of 'Hemoglobin' is found in muscle cells to store oxygen?
e: Myoglobin consists of only one polypeptide chain and has a very high affinity for oxygen.

qe: Which of the following is the 'Universal' first step of respiration that occurs in both aerobic and anaerobic organisms?
e: Glycolysis takes place in the cytoplasm and does not require oxygen to break down glucose into pyruvate.

qe: The total number of ATP molecules produced from one molecule of Glucose during 'Anaerobic' respiration is:
e: In the absence of oxygen, only glycolysis occurs, yielding a net gain of 2 ATP molecules.

qe: Where exactly does the 'Krebs Cycle' (TCA Cycle) take place within the cell?
e: The enzymes for the Krebs cycle are located in the fluid matrix of the mitochondria.

qe: Which molecule acts as the 'Final Electron Acceptor' in the Electron Transport Chain (ETC)?
e: Oxygen combines with electrons and hydrogen ions to form water, allowing the chain to continue.

qe: The 'Respiratory Quotient' (RQ) of Carbohydrates is:
e: RQ is the ratio of CO2 produced to O2 consumed. For glucose, the ratio is exactly 1.0.

qe: During heavy exercise, 'Lactic Acid' buildup in muscles is a result of:
e: When oxygen is low, pyruvate is converted into lactic acid to regenerate NAD+ for glycolysis.

qe: Which of the following is the 'Connecting Link' between Glycolysis and the Krebs Cycle?
e: Pyruvate is decarboxylated and combined with Coenzyme A to form Acetyl CoA before entering the mitochondria.

qe: The 'F0-F1 Particles' (Oxysomes) responsible for ATP synthesis are located on the:
e: These particles contain the enzyme ATP synthase, which uses a proton gradient to create ATP.

qe: What is the 'RQ' value for Fats (Tripalmitin)?
e: Fats require more oxygen for oxidation relative to the CO2 they produce, resulting in an RQ less than 1.

qe: Which chemical is known as the 'Energy Currency' of the cell?
e: Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP) stores and provides energy for almost all cellular activities.

qe: The conversion of Pyruvic acid into Ethyl Alcohol occurs in which organism?
e: Fermentation in yeast produces ethanol and CO2, which is used in the brewing and baking industries.

qe: Which of the following describes 'Oxidative Phosphorylation'?
o: Production of ATP using energy from the Electron Transport Chain
e: It is the final stage of aerobic respiration where the majority of ATP is produced.

qe: How many turns of the Krebs Cycle are required for the complete oxidation of one molecule of Glucose?
e: Since one glucose produces two pyruvate molecules, the Krebs cycle must turn twice.

qe: Which of the following acts as a 'Mobile Electron Carrier' in the mitochondrial membrane?
e: Cytochrome c is a small protein that moves electrons between Complex III and Complex IV.

qe: What is the net gain of NADH molecules from 'Glycolysis' alone?
e: Glycolysis produces 2 ATP (net) and 2 NADH molecules per glucose.

qe: The 'Cyanide' poison kills by inhibiting which part of respiration?
o: Cytochrome c oxidase (Complex IV) of ETC
e: Cyanide stops the Electron Transport Chain, preventing the cell from using oxygen to make ATP.

qe: Which of the following is a 5-carbon compound in the Krebs Cycle?
e: Alpha-ketoglutarate is the only 5-carbon intermediate in the cycle.

qe: What is 'Beta-Oxidation' related to?
o: Breakdown of Fatty Acids for energy
e: Fatty acids are broken down into Acetyl CoA units through beta-oxidation to enter the Krebs cycle.

qe: The enzyme 'Enolase' used in Glycolysis requires which metal ion as a co-factor?
e: Magnesium is a vital co-factor for many enzymes involved in phosphate transfer.

qe: Which part of the 'Atmospheric Air' remains constant in percentage during both inhalation and exhalation?
e: Nitrogen is not used by the body during respiration, so about 78-79% is inhaled and exhaled.

qe: What is the primary physiological adaptation in humans staying at high altitudes for several weeks?
e: The kidneys release Erythropoietin (EPO) to increase RBC count, helping the blood carry more oxygen in low-pressure environments.

qe: During the 'Electron Transport Chain', how many ATP molecules are produced from one molecule of NADH?
e: According to the classical calculation, 1 NADH yields 3 ATP, while 1 FADH2 yields 2 ATP.

qe: What is 'Nitrogen Narcosis' often called by deep-sea divers?
e: At high pressure, nitrogen dissolves in cell membranes, acting like an anesthetic and causing a feeling of euphoria or drunkenness.

qe: Which of the following describes 'Acapnia'?
o: Abnormally low carbon dioxide in the blood
e: Acapnia is usually caused by hyperventilation, which 'washes out' CO2 from the system.

qe: The 'Respiratory Membrane' thickness is approximately:
e: The extremely thin membrane allows for rapid diffusion of gases between the alveoli and the blood.

qe: Which part of the 'Hemoglobin' dissociation curve is affected by 'Carbon Monoxide' (CO)?
o: It shifts to the Left and becomes flatter
e: CO binds to heme 200x stronger than O2 and prevents the remaining O2 from being released to tissues (Left shift).

qe: The total 'Net Gain' of ATP from one molecule of glucose in Aerobic Respiration is roughly:
e: Depending on the shuttle system used (Glycerol phosphate vs Malate-aspartate), the total is 36 or 38 ATP.

qe: What is the 'Oxygen Debt' (Lactic Acid oxygen system)?
o: Extra oxygen needed to process lactic acid after exercise
e: After heavy exercise, the body breathes heavily to restore ATP and convert lactic acid back to glucose in the liver.

qe: Which of the following is a 'Restrictive' lung disease?
e: Restrictive diseases make the lungs 'stiff,' reducing total lung capacity, unlike obstructive diseases which block airflow.

qe: What is the 'P50' value in the Oxygen-Hemoglobin curve?
o: Pressure where 50% of hemoglobin is saturated with O2
e: A higher P50 means lower affinity for oxygen (the curve has shifted to the right).

qe: The 'Hamburger Phenomenon' is essential for maintaining:
e: The chloride shift ensures that the exit of negative bicarbonate ions is balanced by the entry of negative chloride ions.

qe: Which enzyme converts 'Glucose-6-Phosphate' back into 'Glucose' in the liver?
e: This allows the liver to release free glucose into the blood to maintain blood sugar levels during fasting.

qe: What is 'Orthopnea'?
e: Orthopnea is common in patients with heart failure or pulmonary edema.

qe: The 'Maximum Voluntary Ventilation' (MVV) tests the:
o: Strength of respiratory muscles and lung mechanics
e: It measures the maximum amount of air that can be inhaled and exhaled in one minute.

qe: Which molecule is known as the 'Common Oxidative Pathway' for Carbs, Fats, and Proteins?
e: All three macronutrients are eventually converted into Acetyl-CoA to enter the Krebs Cycle.

qe: What is the 'Respiratory Exchange Ratio' (RER) during intense exercise?
e: As exercise intensity increases, the body relies more on carbohydrates, pushing the RER toward 1.0.

qe: Which condition is characterized by 'Barrel Chest'?
e: Chronic air trapping in emphysema causes the rib cage to remain partially expanded all the time.

qe: The 'Venous Admixture' or 'Shunt' refers to:
o: Blood that bypasses the lungs without being oxygenated
e: A small amount of deoxygenated blood always mixes with oxygenated blood, slightly lowering the pO2 of systemic blood.

qe: Which 'Complex' of the ETC is also known as 'Succinate Dehydrogenase'?
e: Complex II is the only enzyme that participates in both the Krebs Cycle and the Electron Transport Chain.

qe: What is 'Kussmaul Breathing'?
o: Deep, labored gasping often seen in Diabetic Ketoacidosis
e: It is a form of hyperventilation that helps the body reduce CO2 levels to compensate for metabolic acidosis.

qe: A 'Pneumothorax' refers to which condition?
o: Air in the pleural cavity causing lung collapse
e: If the chest wall is punctured, air enters the pleural space, neutralizing the negative pressure needed to keep lungs inflated.
